content.text: Restarts are flat (the only pod with a non-zero restart count, `user`, is at 7 in both periods), so rate's silence isn't a restart. Next I'll look at the search→rate client-span durations and search's own metrics.

input.query: SELECT 'abn' src, CASE WHEN duration<1e6 THEN '<1ms' WHEN duration<1e8 THEN '<100ms' WHEN duration<1e9 THEN '<1s' WHEN duration<5e9 THEN '<5s' WHEN duration<1.5e10 THEN '<15s' ELSE '>=15s' END bucket, attr_status_code, count(*) n FROM abnormal_traces WHERE span_name='rate.Rate/GetRates' AND attr_span_kind='Client' GROUP BY 1,2,3 UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', CASE WHEN duration<1e6 THEN '<1ms' WHEN duration<1e8 THEN '<100ms' WHEN duration<1e9 THEN '<1s' WHEN duration<5e9 THEN '<5s' WHEN duration<1.5e10 THEN '<15s' ELSE '>=15s' END, attr_status_code, count(*) FROM normal_traces WHERE span_name='rate.Rate/GetRates' AND attr_span_kind='Client' GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 1,2,3

SELECT 'abn' src, attr_k8s_pod_name pod, metric, round(avg(value),1) av, round(max(value),1) mx, count(*) n FROM abnormal_metrics WHERE attr_k8s_pod_name LIKE 'search%' AND metric IN ('container.memory.working_set','container.cpu.usage','k8s.pod.memory.usage','container.cpu.time') GROUP BY 1,2,3 UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', attr_k8s_pod_name, metric, round(avg(value),1), round(max(value),1), count(*) FROM normal_metrics WHERE attr_k8s_pod_name LIKE 'search%' AND metric IN ('container.memory.working_set','container.cpu.usage','k8s.pod.memory.usage','container.cpu.time') GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 3,1

content.text: Search→rate calls fail almost instantly (359 of 364 under 1 ms), which points away from a slow network path. I'll look at the failing spans' attributes and at the metric catalogue for any per-connection network data.

content.text: The rate pod stays up and its CPU is flat, but nearly all of its server spans disappear; search's calls into it fail within a millisecond. Before settling on the fault, I'll check whether the frontend's traffic drop is explained by the search failures, by comparing the route mix normal vs abnormal.

input.query: SELECT 'abn' src, span_name, count(*) n, sum(CASE WHEN attr_http_response_status_code>=500 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) http5xx, round(avg(duration)/1e6,2) avg_ms FROM abnormal_traces WHERE service_name='frontend' AND attr_span_kind='Server' GROUP BY 1,2 UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', span_name, count(*), sum(CASE WHEN attr_http_response_status_code>=500 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), round(avg(duration)/1e6,2) FROM normal_traces WHERE service_name='frontend' AND attr_span_kind='Server' GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 2,1

SELECT p.service_name parent_svc, c.service_name child_svc, c.span_name, count(*) n FROM normal_traces c JOIN normal_traces p ON c.parent_span_id = p.span_id AND c.trace_id = p.trace_id WHERE c.attr_span_kind='Client' GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 4 DESC

content.text: The frontend's `/hotels` route is the only one that changed character: all 301 abnormal requests return 500, and the other routes shrink in proportion. Before concluding, I'll check the geo memory shift the survey flagged at 2,460 sigma, since it could be a second fault.
